answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks when identity costs something the attacker cannot fake. Work waits on the pulse until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the lagoon of the next round. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, capped per identity per epoch, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Reaching the glacier of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
